system.description:
Miles punches his training log for the thousandth time today, punching the core of the tree at this point. His teacher walks onto the training field telling Miles to get some rest, it won’t come easier without sleep. Miles turns towards his teacher and begins to focus as chakra begins to swirl around his body. His teacher sees what he’s doing “Miles! Stop! You gonna~”. He stops mid-sentence as he notices that Miles has done it. He has unlocked the 3rd Inner gate. Potential is limitless when you're not bound by preconceived notions of success and expectations.

—Tatsunami Aburame

The Long Road, Ch. 1 excerpt.

Limitless Potential

Those who are a part of no bloodline or large recognized family are known as Non-Clanners or Non-Clan for short. They are the most numerous of the Naruto World and are the primary people who end up creating new clans and families for generations to come. They show the most potential and have the largest room for growth. They don’t have many limitations in regards to what’s expected of them so they have the freedom to try new things and build an identity unique to themselves.

Non-Clan Traits

Ability Score Increase: +2 to any Ability Score, +1 to any other Ability Score (or +1 to any 3 Ability Scores.).

Speed: 30 feet.

Skill Proficiencies: Pick any 3 Skills to gain proficiency in.

Self-Taught Skills: Select two skills you have proficiency in, you gain 1 Rank of Mastery in those skills.

Though Blood, Sweat and Tears: Reduce the Ryo cost to learn and create Jutsu to 0. Also, reduce the Downtime cost to learn and create jutsu by an amount equal to the rank of the jutsu. (D-Rank: -1, C-Rank: -2, B-Rank: -3, A-Rank: -4, S-Rank: -5)

Unrelenting Focus: Select one Feat that you qualify for. You gain an additional Feat choice at 7th and 15th levels.

Non-Clan Features

Limitless Potential

1st Level Clan Feature

You were born with no special family name. No bloodline. No Hijutsu. No Kekkei Genkai. You were born with nothing, but the unending drive for greatness beyond those who were born with it all. You wake up every day with one goal in mind. To surpass everyone else. You accomplish this in two distinct ways, your Drive and your Style.

Drive

Your grit and tenacity in combat is called your Drive, a measure of you building momentum, focus and experience through an encounter. You begin each combat with 0 Drive, and can accumulate up to 1 + Your Proficiency bonus at any given time, resetting to 0 when combat ends.

You gain 1 Drive, when you deal damage to, or take damage from a hostile creature. You can only gain Drive, in either way, once each, until the start of your next turn.

Feature cannot grant you Drive more than once before the start of each of your next turns, unless otherwise specified.

As you build Drive, over the course of combat, you gain passive bonuses based on that accumulated value, can spend it on effects and abilities that call for it. You cannot gain Drive as part of the same action or feature that you spend Drive on.

Momentum Shift – 2+ Drive: Once per turn, when you deal or take damage, you can move up to half your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks and can spend 1 Drive to either; Use a skill-based action, Use the Help action or make one unarmed or weapon attack against a creature in range (Pick one).

Drive Dice – 4+ Drive: Once per turn, you can spend 2 Drive to add a d4 to provide a bonus or penalty to any attack roll, damage roll, or Ability or skill check made by an ally or hostile creature within 30 feet of you. This die is added before the roll resolves. Once you add a bonus or penalty dice to a creatures result, you cannot do so again, for that creature, until the end of your next turn. The power of this penalty increases to a d6 at 11th level.

Apex Drive – 6+ Drive: Your unlock your styles Apex effect, for the remainder of combat.

Style

At character creation, select one of the following Styles.. This Style determines how you generate Drive and what unique abilities you have to spend your Drive on. Each Style grants you a way to generate Drive, a unique special ability and your Apex Drive. This choice cannot be changed later.

Blazing Style. Embodied by those who fights with unmatched aggression and focus (Ex. Rock Lee, Might Guy, Zabuza). Attacks you make gain Pierce 4.

Drive Charge: You can gain 2 Drive on a critical hit.

Blazing Surge: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Drive, converting it into a single charge of an expendable resource your class has (Genjutsu Specialist: Actualization Die, Hunter-Nin: Combat Exploit forgoing Lethal Attack die, Medical-Nin: Domain Charges, etc.).

Apex Drive: When you unlock this effect, select one hostile creature, and select one Damage type or condition. Damage you deal ignores resistance of the chosen damage type. The target creature cannot make saving throws to resist the chosen condition at advantage.

Adamant Style. Embodied by those who endure what others cannot (Sakura, Tsunade). For every Drive you have at the beginning of each of your turns, you gain +2 Temporary hit points. If you have temporary hit points granted by another effect when this feature would activate, you instead gain half of the listed amount, adding it to your current temporary hit point value

Drive Charge: You can gain 2 Drive when you reduce a triggering damage source by half or more.

Enduring Surge: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 2 Drive, selecting one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, until the end of your next turn, the first time each turn you take damage from this creature, reduce the number of damage dice rolled by 1. This increases to 2 at 7th and 3 15th levels.

Apex Drive: You refuse to fall in battle, you must endure. Each time you would fail a saving throw, you can spend 1 Drive to gain a rank of Mastery to the result. You can do this twice per failure.

Guiding Star Style. Embodied by those whose strength multiplies through the bonds they share with their allies (Iruka, Shizune, Sai). All allied creatures, excluding yourself, within 15 feet of you gain a +2 bonus to their damage rolls as your presence sharpen their focus. This increases to +4 at 11th level.

Drive Charge You can gain 2 Drive when you support an allied creature, other than yourself by increasing or restoring any dice-based result (Attack, Damage, Save, etc.), any statistic they have (DR, HP, Chakra, etc.) or reducing incoming damage they take. Other supportive effects can trigger this at GM’s discretion such as interposing an attack or interrupting a harmful jutsu.

Guiding Surge: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Drive, selecting one allied creature. That creature can reroll the next 2 dice rolls they make. Once a creature benefits from this surge, they cannot do so again until they complete a short rest. This increases to 3 dice rolls at 11th level.

Apex Drive: You can use the Help Action targeting any allied creature, as a Bonus action, so long as they are within 60 feet of you. Additionally, when a creature benefits from this Help action, you gain temporary chakra points equal to half your level. You can only temporary chakra in this way, once per creature assisted, per short rest.

Shogi Style. Embodied by those who win battles through preparation, positioning and anticipation before a fight begins. (Temari, Hayate, Jiraiya). Ninja tools you used such as Explosive Tools, Medical Tools, Toolkits, Poisons or Scrolls can be used as a Bonus Action, if their normal use requires an Action.

Drive Charge: You can gain 2 Drive when a hostile creature gains a Condition.

Tactical Surge: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Drive, to summon any one; Weapon, Explosive Tool, Trap, Toolkit, Communication Tool, Blank Keycard or Data Scroll of a rank you can access normally. These Ninja tools can be used once before breaking or expiring or 1 hour has passed, whichever occurs first.

Apex Drive: You always overprepare and overdeliver. Once per creature, per rest, when you cast a Jutsu you know, that you have not previously cast this combat, you can shock your opponent with the gravity of the technique. If they attempt to spend their Reaction in response to the Jutsu, its effects or as part of making or failing a saving throw, you can spend your Reaction, causing them to lose their Reaction.

Wayfarer

1st Level Clan Feature

You have to work harder to move in combat than your peers. You don’t have inherent special movement abilities like the Namikaze, Jiton or Hoshigaki. You weren’t born special. You had to work for yours. This is expressed in the following mobility options. You select one, selecting an additional option at 11th levels.

Surface Step

Your ability to adhere to a surface with chakra is exceptionally refined. When Wall or Water Walking, you no longer spend additional movement per foot traveled, allowing you to move at your full speed on walls, ceilings and across water. Additionally, you no longer make saving throws and checks to resist being knocked prone, pushed or pulled at disadvantage while Wall or Water Walking.

Deep Diver

Your Chakra control extends to your respiratory system. Double the length of time you can hold your breath both in and out of combat. Additionally, you gain a Swim speed equal to your movement speed.

Quick Shift

Your footwork has been refined to handle most hostile surfaces. Terrain that deals damage to you as you move through it is less effective against you. Reduce the damage you take from such terrain by 5. If you have DR, you can choose to instead apply your DR to the damage of this terrain.

Off Center Assault

While Wall Walking, if you make a melee attack against a creature that is not Wall Walking on the same surface, you overwhelm them with an assault from an angle they aren’t used to fending off. These attacks deal an additional 1d6 damage on a hit.

Silent Cross

While Wall Walking, Water Walking, Swimming or Burrowing, your movement is silent, making no sound. Creatures attempting to perceive you using sound make their checks at disadvantage. You are invisible to creatures using Tremor sense while using one of the listed special movements.

Flow State

When entering any form of special movement, you do not spend the normal 10 feet of movement to activate said special movement, allowing you to move between different special forms of movement with ease compared to other shinobi who are slowed down with each transition.

Chakra Suppressed Steps

While using Wall or Water Walking, you cannot be seen by Chakra Sight passively. A creature can only see you with Chakra Sight if they are performing the Search skill action and beating your Passive Stealth or Stealth DC, whichever is higher.

Living Shadow

Once per turn, on your turn, while in dim light or darkness, you can spend 10 feet of your movement to attempt the Hide skill action. Additionally, when you are Sneaking you can move up to your full speed.

Nindo

3rd Level Clan Feature

You are not someone who gives in easily. You have created a short saying to yourself, something you repeat to yourself when you are in a tight spot and when your backs against the wall. This saying is your Nindo, your Ninja way, and you repeat it when things get tough. You select one Nindo phrase reflavoring it to fit your shinobi, gaining its effects. You expand your horizons at 7th and 15th level, being inspired by your mentors, allies and clients, gaining an additional Nindo, at the select levels.

Never Back Down

This Nindo is one of tenacity. When an you gain a Physical or Mental Condition, you did not have ranks of already from a hostile effect, you gain 1 Drive. If you spend 1 Drive on your turn, you gain advantage on the first attack roll and saving throw you make before the beginning of your next turn.

Never Give up

This Nindo is one of perseverance. When you Clash with a hostile creature, you gain 2 Drive and a rank of Mastery to this Clash check.

Additionally, once per long rest, when you roll a Death saving throw, you can spend 2 Drive as part of rolling a success, you treat it as if you had succeeded twice.

Never Abandon A Friend

This Nindo is one of compassion. When an allied creature that you can reach within half of your movement speed takes damage, you can spend your reaction and 2 Drive to move up to half your speed towards them, redirect the damage to yourself, and if possible cast a Jutsu with a casting time of Reaction, when you take damage as part of this reaction.

Additionally, if an allied creature is Dying and you attempt to stabilize them, you make the check at advantage. On a success, they regain hit points equal to your level. You can heal a dying creature in this way once per long rest, per creature.

Never lose a Fight

This Nindo is one of power. When you lose a clash with a hostile creature, you can choose to spend 2 Drive. When you do, you treat this clash as if it were a draw.

Additionally, when you roll initiative fighting a hostile creature whose level is 2 or higher than your own, you gain 2 Will of Fire. If you have not used these Will of Fire before the end of combat, you lose them.

Never Fail

This Nindo is one of resilience. Once per turn, when you fail a saving throw that would deal damage to you, you can spend 2 Drive to remake the failed saving throw. If you spend 5 Drive, you can instead choose to automatically succeed, suffering no damage or effects that would be applied on a success.

Never Give In

This Nindo is one of resolve. When an ally is reduced to 0 hit points that you can see, you can spend 3 Drive. When you do, at the end of your next turn, you immediately take an additional turn. You gain 3 ranks of Exhaustion at the end of that additional turn.

Always Finish What I Start

This Nindo is one of conviction. Once per turn, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain 2 Drive, even if you gained Drive already this turn and can move up to half your speed towards another hostile creature. If you end this movement with that creature within your weapons range, you can make one weapon attack targeting them, dealing 2d6 bonus damage on a hit.

Always Move First

This Nindo is one of preparation. When you roll initiative, mark each hostile creature whose result is lower than yours until the end of your next turn. The first time you deal damage to a marked creature as a result of an attack, you can treat the attack as a critical hit, causing the creature to lose their mark.

Always Protect What Matters

This Nindo is one of purpose. When an allied creature within 30 feet is hit by a critical attack or fails a saving throw, you can spend your reaction to cast a D-Rank jutsu with a casting time of 1 Action, targeting the assailing creature, forcing a Clash.

Always Save Who I can

This Nindo is one of healing. When you cast a Jutsu or use a feature that restores an allied creatures, excluding yourself, hit points, you can spend 2 Drive to mark them as Saved, for the next minute. A Saved creature that gains ranks of a condition from a hostile effect, reduced the ranks they would gain by 1, losing the Saved mark.

Always Fix What is Broken

This Nindo is one of restoration. When you cast a jutsu or use a feature that removed a Condition from an allied creature you can spend 2 Drive to mark them as Fixed for the next minute. A Fixed creature is treated as they have resistance to the condition originally removed by you.

Always Go Beyond

This Nindo is one of evolution. The first time you fall below half your maximum hit or chakra points, you can choose to enter your Ultra Focus state. Once you enter this state, you cannot re-enter it until you complete a short rest.

| #### Ultra Focus / Fortitude Amp / Your back is against the wall and you need to focus, going beyond what your limits suggest; / Uncapped Strength. You gain a +2 bonus to damage you deal. This increases to +4 at 11th level. / Broken Limits. Once per turn on your turn, you can spend 3 Drive, spending your Bonus Action, to gain an Action. / Always Push Forward. You gain advantage on saving throws and checks to resist being Grappled, Restrained, Stunned, Staggered having your speed reduced by hostile effects. / Stress. At the end of each of your turns, make a Constitution ability check vs a DC 20. On a success, you persist in this state and it doesn’t end. On a failure, this state ends. |

Chosen Path

3rd Level Clan Feature

Every shinobi arrives at a crossroad. The one that makes them choose a path of focus. The ones born into clans never have to make this choice. It was made for them as a result of their bloodline. But you aren’t one of them, you’ve speed unspoken time watching learning and determining which discipline is the one you will follow. Select one of the following Paths. This decision cannot be changed later.

Path of Ninshou

You’ve decided to focus on chakra molding and Ninjutsu.

Chakra Imprint. As a Bonus action on your turn, you can imprint a target creature within 60 feet of you with your chakra, until the end of your next turn. An imprinted creature, cannot make saving throws against jutsu you cast at advantage.

Chakra Anchor. When you deal damage to a creature, you can spend 2 Drive to restrain their presence. Until the end of your next turn, the affected creature cannot teleport or be moved by jutsu or feature based effects that does not spend their movement.

Path of the Fist

You’ve decided to focus on hardening your body, fists and feet.

Unrelenting Strikes. You unarmed attacks gain the Deadly 2 weapon property.

Combat Rhythm. When you deal damage to a creature with a Taijutsu you cast that doesn’t have either the Combo or Finisher keywords, you can spend 2 Drive to give the jutsu the Combo keyword.

Path of the Magician

You’ve decided to focus on breaking the minds of your foes.

Cold Illusion. Once per turn, when you score a hit with an attack against a creature, you can conjure an illusory doppelganger of yourself in any unoccupied space within 15 feet of you, has 10 AC, 1 Hit Point and lasts until the beginning of your next turn. While active and within 15 feet of you, the first time a hostile creature targets you, they must make a Wisdom saving throw vs your Genjutsu save DC. On a failure, they target the doppelganger instead.

Illusory Tools. As part of casting a Genjutsu, you can spend 2 Drive to conjure one illusory Explosive Tool or ranged weapon, throwing it at the same target, either making an attack if a weapon, or following the rules of the chosen tool if it forces a saving throw. If the tool deals damage, the damage becomes psychic damage.

Path of the Blade

You’ve decided that a sharp or sturdy weapon is your best tool.

Twisting Turn. Once per turn, when you deal [Weapon Damage] to a hostile creature, you can make one additional attack using a Kunai, Shuriken or Senbon. If you score a hit with this attack, you force the target creature to make a Dexterity saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, they gain a rank of Bruised until the end of your next turn.

Chain Break. As part of Casting a Bukijutsu with the Chain keyword, by spending 2 Drive, you can select which chain rank you want to use. Once you use this ability, you cannot benefit from the chain effect of a Bukijutsu you cast, until the end of your next turn. You can still sustain a chain as normal.

Universal Path

You’ve decided that dedicating yourself to a strict path is foolish. You choose to be flexible instead of rigid.

Self-Mastery. For every jutsu you cast beyond the first one cast on a turn, with a casting discipline keyword different from the previous jutsu cast this same turn, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage dealt, stacking up to three times.

Open Form. As part of Casting a Ninjutsu, Genjutsu, Taijutsu or Bukijutsu, you can spend 2 Drive. When you do, you can spend either your Bonus Action or Reaction to gain an additional Action, which can only be used to cast one of the remaining casting discipline jutsu. If you do, you can spend an additional 2 Drive, to spend the remaining Bonus action or Reaction to gain an additional Action to cast one of the remaining casting discipline jutsu that you have not cast this turn. These castings must target different creatures, unless there is a Solo Adversary in combat, in which case these castings must target that creature.

One of Us

7th Level Clan Feature

You carry no clan name, no family crest and no inherited title that speaks before you do. To the merchants, farmers and laborers you are one of them, even if you wear a headband. When engaging in a social encounter with a creature that doesn’t carry a clan name or is of noble heritage, they have a softer attitude towards you because you feel relatable. Their Attitude towards you increases by +1, unless they are familiar with you or have a personal reason not see you as relatable.

Additionally, when you spend at least 10 minutes engaging with common folk in a settlement, outpost or populated area, you can tap into the whispers of these people, learning one of the following, GM Choice.

The name and whereabouts of one Criminal, Underground or Black-market contact in the area.

One rumor, secret or piece of information about a local clan, noble or authority figure that the common folk are aware of, but never speak openly about.

The current mood, tension or political situation among the common people, such as fear, unrest, or brewing conflict that authority figures are unaware of.

Righteous Growth

11th Level Clan Feature

You have grown. Through your choices, decisions, faults and failures. You have survived countless fights, and have learned from them the righteous way to forge your own path. You develop another way to build Drive, select one between Teamwork and Mobility. Regardless of this choice, you also gain 2 additional ways to spend your Drive.

Build Drive

Teamwork. Once per turn, when an allied creature provides you a boost to a roll you make, cleanse you of a condition, restores your hit points or chakra point, or uses an effect that provides you advantage or any other form of assistance in combat, you gain 2 Drive. Other supportive effects can trigger this at GM’s discretion such as them interposing an attack or interrupting a harmful jutsu.

Mobility. Once per turn, when you transition to using a form of special movement such as Wall or Water Walking, Swimming, Climbing or Burrowing, before making an attack or casting a jutsu on the same turn, you gain 1 Drive.

Spend Drive

Battle Insight. You can study a hostile creature you can see within 60 feet of you, using your accumulated battle experience to gather information normally invisible to you. By spending 1 Drive, and a Bonus action, you gain one of the following pieces of information.

One random Damage or Condition immunity, resistance or vulnerability they have.

Their DR.

Their Highest Saving throw, and its bonus.

Their highest Jutsu attack Bonus and Save DC.

One special action or ability they have.

Recover. You can spend Drive in multiples of 2, up to your remaining. For every 2 Drive spent this way, you remove 1 rank of any Physical, Sensory or Mental condition currently affecting you.

One Who Endures

15th Level Clan Feature

You’ve spent your whole life being compared to those with legacies, and told you were behind. But you’ve spent that time building yourself from nothing, to reach the peak of a world that expected nothing of you. You have become the one who endures.

Beginning at 15th level, whenever you would gain Drive from any Non-Clan feature, you gain +1 additional drive. Additionally, you gain immunity to the Demoralized and Shaken conditions as you can no longer be perturbed by anything other than disappointing yourself.
